It was said: the pronoun in ﴿la'allahu﴾ refers to the disbeliever. That is, you hoped that he would purify himself through Islam, or be mindful, so that the reminder would bring him close to accepting the truth; and what makes you know that what you hoped for will come to pass?

It is also read as ﴿fa-tanfa'ahu﴾ (so that it benefits him) in the nominative, coordinated with ﴿yadhdhakkaru﴾ (he is mindful), and in the accusative as an answer to ﴿la'alla﴾ (perhaps), like His saying ﴿fa-aṭṭali'a ilā ilāhi Mūsā﴾ (so that I may look upon the god of Moses). ﴿Taṣaddā﴾ means to present oneself by turning attention toward him, and taṣādī means opposition. It is also read as tuṣaddī with shadda, by assimilating the tā' into the ṣād. Abu Ja'far read tuṣaddā with a ḍamma on the tā', meaning: presents himself. Its meaning: a caller calls you to pursue him, out of eagerness and intense desire for his Islam; and there is no blame on you that he does not purify himself through Islam.

﴿You are not responsible except for conveying the message.﴾ ﴿He comes eagerly﴾ - he hastens in seeking good, ﴿and he fears [Allah]﴾ - or fears the disbelievers and their harm in coming to you. It was said: he came without a guide, so he feared stumbling. ﴿You distract yourself﴾ - you occupy yourself, from "lahiya 'anhu" and "talahha" and "tataallā". Talha ibn Musarrif read tatalahhā. I say: Yes, and its meaning is the denial of presenting oneself and being distracted toward him; that is, someone like you in particular should not present himself to the rich and be distracted from the poor.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 80, verse 41:

It is said: "Sakhkha li-hadithihi" (he listened attentively to his speech), like "asakha lahu" (he gave ear to him). The Blast (al-nafkha) is therefore described metaphorically as al-Sakhkha (the Deafening Blast), because people give ear to it (yasukhhuna lahu). A man flees from them (yafirru minhum) because he is occupied with what has been committed to him, and because he knows that they will not avail him anything.

He begins with the brother, then the parents, because they are nearer to him, then the spouse and the children, because they are nearer and dearer, as if He said: he flees from his brother, nay, from his parents, nay, from his spouse and his children. It is also said: he flees from them out of fear of being pursued for their dues (al-tab'at).

The brother says: "You did not share your wealth with me." The parents say: "You fell short in dutifulness to us." The spouse says: "You fed me the unlawful and did and made such-and-such." The children say: "You did not teach us and did not guide us." It is also said: the first from whom he flees is his brother, Habil; from his parents, Ibrahim; from his spouse, Nuh and Lut; and from his son, Nuh.

Yughnihi (﴿يُغْنِيهِ﴾): suffices him, i.e., is enough for him in being concerned about him. It has also been read as yu'nihi (﴿يُعْنِيهِ﴾), meaning it concerns him (yahummuhu).

Musfirah (﴿مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾): bright, radiant, glowing, from asfara al-subh (the dawn lit up) when it shone.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him both, that it means: from the night prayer, because of what is narrated in the hadith: "Whoever's prayer at night is abundant, his face becomes beautiful by day" [[Mentioned earlier in the commentary on Surah al-Fath.]]. It is related from al-Dahhak: from the traces of wudu' (ablution).

It has been said: ﴿غَبَرَةٌ﴾ (dust) that covers them from the long time they were dusted in the way of Allah. ﴿قَتَرَةٌ﴾ (darkness) is blackness like smoke. Nothing is more desolate than the combination of dust and blackness on the face, as you see in the faces of the Zanj (Black people) when they become dusty. It is as if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, adds dust to the blackness of their faces, just as they combined immorality with disbelief.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah 'Abasa wa-tawalla, will come on the Day of Resurrection with a face laughing and joyful." [[Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
